title: Fixture expectation
description: The derived expectation for one scored fixture. Written by tools/fixtures/derive.py and read by src/tda/eval/expectation.py. Neither side may import the other, so this file is the contract between them: a change here is a change both packages must follow, and the schema is validated on write and on read so a drift fails loudly rather than scoring against a stale shape. Every figure is a decimal STRING, never a JSON number, because the pipeline compares Decimals and a float round-trip would reintroduce the drift the tolerance policy exists to make explicit.

fixture_set_version.description: tools.fixtures.FIXTURE_SET_VERSION at derivation time. The scorer refuses a fixture derived by a different version rather than scoring against an expectation whose meaning may have moved.

why.description: What this fixture defends against, in a sentence. Carried into the eval report so a reader of the scorecard does not have to open the spec.

mutation.description: The mutation as declared, echoed for the report. The scorer never reasons from this: everything it asserts is in `status`, `findings` and `definitional_items`, already derived. Present so a failing fixture can be read without opening the spec.

status.description: The expected VerdictStatus. Asserted separately from each finding's escalates_to: a run that halted for an unrelated reason would otherwise satisfy F6 by accident.

exhaustive.description: The finding lists are complete. The scorer asserts set equality against the verdict, not containment, which is what makes a false positive on a control fixture a failure rather than an unnoticed extra.

findings.description: Non-definitional findings, matching Verdict.findings. A V2 here is a contract violation on both sides.

definitional_items.description: V2 only, matching Verdict.definitional_items. Kept separate because the verdict keeps them separate: a definitional disagreement is not a hotel error and must not be filed as one.

key.description: MetricKey.rendered, e.g. guests_by_nationality:2026-01:nationality_iso2=DE. The join key between expectation and verdict; finding ids are minted per run and cannot be predicted.

claimed.description: Decimal as a string. Null where the workbook omitted the figure (D-MAT-04).

computed.description: Decimal as a string. Null where no source value could be established (V7).

proposed_correction.description: Non-null for V1 only. Proposing a corrected value for a definitional variance would tell a hotel to change a number that is not wrong.

evidence.description: What a reviewer can open. At most one side may be a typed absence; both absent is refused by the Finding contract and must never be derived.

oneOf.description: A typed absence. Legitimate for a V5 whose claimed value is null, and for a V7.

source.description: What the claim was checked against. `pdf_page` asserts a PdfRef carrying a page and a row range, without pinning which page: the page a figure derives from is the extractor's to determine, and pinning it here would make the expectation a second implementation of extraction. `inventory_ref` asserts an InventoryRef, which carries a file and a data row range and deliberately has no page. It is not an alternative spelling of pdf_page: D-RNA-01 makes rooms available a property attribute rather than a reservation attribute, so it is absent from the reservation export and arrives in a separate CSV. Collapsing the two would make a correct citation read as a wrong page.
